paragraphs: The ML270 CDI was introduced in 1999 as a diesel option for the first-generation M-Class. It uses the OM612 — a 2.7-litre five-cylinder diesel that was part of Mercedes' CDI (Common-rail Direct Injection) family. This engine was fitted throughout the W163 generation's production run, from 1999 until the M-Class was replaced by the W164 generation in 2005.
about.boldParagraph: We continue to rebuild and replace M256 engines for every ML270 CDI on the road.

cards.body: A 3.0-litre inline-six petrol mild-hybrid engine fitted to the ML270 CDI from 2023 to present. The M256 features an integrated starter-generator (ISG) and electric auxiliary compressor, making it a more modern and efficient design than the older M276 V6. We replace timing chains, bearings, water pump and gaskets as standard on every M256 rebuild.
